Rory McIlroy will be playing in Australia this summer. (Getty Images: PGA Tour/Ben Jared)

Rory McIlroy's appearance at the Australian Open and Australian PGA Championship headlines the 19-event PGA Tour of Australasia schedule.

Officials have revealed they have been targeting two-time US Open winner Bryson DeChambeau for the PGA Championship in Sydney.

The season begins this month with the PNG Open on August 27–30.

The return of grand slam winner Rory McIlroy and the first Australian PGA Championship in Sydney this century highlights a 19-event summer of golf starting this month.

With the global professional golf scene in a state of flux, the Australasian Tour has secured a record partnership and announced a jam-packed schedule with major championship and European Tour spots once again up for grabs.

McIlroy back gracing Melbourne fairways, this time at iconic Kingston Heath from December 3–6, and the PGA Championship at The Lakes possibly featuring big-hitting fan favourite Bryson DeChambeau, are the two hottest tickets.

Rory McIlroy's appearance at the Australian Open in Melbourne has gone a long way to restoring the prestige of the tournament.

Record crowds followed the Northern Irishman at last year's Australian Open at Royal Melbourne before McIlroy successfully defended his US Masters title at Augusta National in April.

Officials revealed they were also targeting two-time US Open winner DeChambeau for the PGA, which was last held in Sydney back in 1998.

The new season begins in the now traditional style with the PNG Open at Royal Port Moresby Golf Club on August 27–30 before visiting all mainland states in Australia, as well as New Zealand's north and south islands, across the 19-tournament schedule.

The centenary Queensland PGA Championship will take place on the Kurrai course at Nudgee Golf Club in Brisbane from November 19–22.

Boasting a past champions list that includes Australian greats Greg Norman, David Graham and Peter Senior, the event will be played immediately before the Australian PGA Championship.

Co-sanctioned by the European Tour, the Australian PGA Championship also marks the start of the Race to Dubai, the tour's season-long rankings competition.

The PGA Tour of Australasia will also feature two new tournament venues in 2026–27.

Secret Harbour Golf Links, south of Perth, will host the WA Open for the first time, while Peninsula Kingswood Country Golf Club becomes the new home of Players Series Victoria as a forerunner to hosting next year's Australian Open.

There is a switch of order for the three-leg New Zealand swing in February that proved to be a huge success in 2026.

The New Zealand Open will now be the finale, following the Japan-Australasia Championship that returns for its second year at Royal Auckland & Grange Golf Club.
